chunks: I was with my master Abu 'Abd Allah (peace be upon him): a man complained to him of a need. He said: 'Be patient, for Allah (Glorious is His Majesty) will make relief for you.' Then he was silent for a while, then he turned to the man and said: 'Tell me about the prison of Al-Kufah, how is it?' He said: 'May Allah rectify you, it is narrow and foul-smelling, and its inmates are in the worst of conditions.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'You are in a prison too, you want to be at ease. Do you not know that the world is the prison of the believer?'
ai.seo_question: What is the meaning of the world being a prison for the believer?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) uses the physical confinement of Al-Kufah’s prison as a metaphor to illustrate the spiritual reality that the world is a prison for the believer, a concept deeply rooted in Shia eschatology. This narration, found in *Kitab al-Mumin*, emphasizes that enduring worldly afflictions with patience is not merely a test but a means of attaining ultimate freedom and divine relief in the Hereafter.

en.muhajir-b-ali: I was with my master Abu 'Abd Allah (a.s) when a man complained to him (of a need). 'Be patient,' he (a.s) told him, 'for Allah will give you relief.' Then he (al-Sadiq (a.s)) remained silent for a while. Then he turned towards the man and said, 'Tell me about the prison of Al-Kufah, how is it?' 'May Allah protect you,' the man replied, 'It is confining in space, putrid in smell and its inmates are in the worst of conditions.' 'But you are in a prison too,' retorted Abu 'Abd Allah (a.s), 'Do you expect to be at ease? Do you not know that the world is a prison for the believer?'
